# M0-2a: MCP SDK + OAuth choice, hello server with Google sign-in (local)

- Milestone: M0
- Branch / worktree: `t/M0-2a`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M0-2a`
- Depends on: none (BA-5 done)
- Touches (exclusive while running): `spikes/mcp/`, `docs/build/spikes/mcp.md`
- Plan refs: architecture.md §4 (Remote MCP); §9 U8, U9; requirements.md N6, N7, N9 only
- YNAB access: none
- Deploy: no (M0-2b deploys this server to hoid)

## Goal
Pick the MCP Go SDK and an OAuth approach that we don't hand-roll, and prove them locally. Done means a hello MCP server on
this Mac that an MCP client can connect to over Streamable HTTP, after the user signs in with Google. Only allowlisted Google
accounts get through. The output is a working spike that M0-2b deploys, plus a findings doc.

## Setup facts (verified by sup 2026-10-29)
- `.env` (copied into your worktree) has `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` for a Google **Web
  application** client in project `finbot`. The consent screen is External, in **Testing** mode, with only Brendan and his
  wife as test users. Never print either value.
- The registered redirect URI is exactly `http://localhost:8080/oauth/google/callback`. Use that path. finbot's own OAuth
  endpoints for MCP clients live elsewhere under `/oauth/*` or the well-known paths. M0-2b adds
  `https://finance.<domain>/oauth/google/callback`.
- Allowlist: read it from env `MCP_ALLOWED_EMAILS` (comma-separated). sup has set it to Brendan's address only. Compare
  against the **verified** email claim (`email_verified=true`) from Google's ID token. Never commit or log the addresses; log a
  short hash if you need to.
- Local toolchain: Go 1.25.7 (a spike module may declare a newer `go` line; the toolchain auto-downloads). Node 23 and `npx`
  are available for MCP Inspector.

## Scope
- **SDK choice (U8):** compare the official `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` with `mark3labs/mcp-go`. Cover:
  - Streamable HTTP server support;
  - auth hooks: bearer-token middleware, protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728);
  - release maturity and version;
  - spec revision supported.
  
  Pick one and record the exact version.
- **OAuth approach:** choose among the options in §4:
  - (a) a library-based authorization server kept minimal (e.g. `ory/fosite`);
  - (b) an external AS in front;
  - (c) the SDK's own auth helpers.
  
  Do NOT hand-roll token issuing or validation crypto. The criteria are:
  - works end to end with Claude.ai custom connectors, which need the spec's discovery: RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata,
    RFC 8414 AS metadata, and Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591) and/or whatever claude.ai currently documents;
  - revocation in one step;
  - the smallest code we own.
  
  Cite the claude.ai custom-connector auth docs you relied on.
- **Hello server** under `spikes/mcp/` (its own `go.mod`; root module untouched), listening on `localhost:8080`:
  - MCP endpoint (e.g. `/mcp`) with one read tool `hello` that returns the caller's identity, as a hashed email or a display
    name, never the raw email. That proves the auth context reaches tool handlers.
  - The AS flow delegates login to Google (authorization code + PKCE). Map the Google identity → allowlist → finbot-issued
    token. Reject non-allowlisted accounts with a clear error.
  - Unauthenticated `/mcp` returns 401 with a correct `WWW-Authenticate` header pointing at the resource metadata.
  - Revocation: one command or flag that invalidates a user's tokens, e.g. a signing-key rotation or a per-user token
    generation counter. Show that it works.
  - Config entirely from env; tokens and keys only in memory or a gitignored file under `spikes/mcp/`.
- **Local end-to-end:** connect with MCP Inspector (`npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector`) and, if practical, with Claude
  Code (`claude mcp add --transport http …` in a scratch scope, not the repo's settings). Brendan has to complete the Google
  sign-in in his browser: when ready, append `QUESTION M0-2a: please sign in at <url/steps>` to your signal file and wait
  (poll your log, don't spin). After the sign-in, call `hello` and show the result.
- **Clients (U9):** research which AI apps support remote MCP with OAuth and DCR: Claude web, mobile and desktop; ChatGPT;
  Gemini. Cite official docs and label each VERIFIED or UNVERIFIED. M0-2b tests the real connectors.
- Write `docs/build/spikes/mcp.md`:
  - the SDK comparison and choice;
  - the OAuth option and why;
  - the endpoints and the flow (a sequence list);
  - the token format and lifetime;
  - the revocation method;
  - the client support table;
  - what M0-2b must verify on hoid, including proxy headers, the public issuer URL and the second redirect URI;
  - a recommendation;
  - an "Impact on architecture" section (§4).
- Unit tests for the allowlist check and for the 401 / `WWW-Authenticate` behaviour.

## Out of scope
- Deploying to hoid, nginx or DNS (M0-2b). Any YNAB access. Real finbot tools.
- Changing the Google Cloud client or consent screen. If you need a change (another redirect URI, a scope), signal a
  QUESTION for Brendan.
- Scopes beyond `openid email profile`. Storing Google refresh tokens.
- Root module, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/plan/*`. Committing emails, client ids or secrets, tokens, or real issuer keys.

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] `cd spikes/mcp && go run .` serves on `localhost:8080`. `curl -i localhost:8080/mcp` → 401 with `WWW-Authenticate`
      (show it). The well-known metadata endpoints return valid JSON (show it, redacted).
- [ ] A real Google sign-in by Brendan through MCP Inspector (or Claude Code) ends with a successful `hello` call (show the
      redacted output). A non-allowlisted identity is rejected: show it, by test or by temporarily emptying the allowlist.
- [ ] Revocation demonstrated: a token works, revoke, the same token → 401.
- [ ] `docs/build/spikes/mcp.md` has every section listed in Scope, with VERIFIED/UNVERIFIED labels and cited sources.
- [ ] The branch diff contains no secrets, client id, emails or tokens (grep it and show the check).
- [ ] Spike module `go vet ./... && go test ./...` green; root `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` still green.

## Result
- Status: DONE
- What changed:
  - `spikes/mcp/` (own module): a hello MCP server on go-sdk **v1.8.0** (Streamable HTTP, `auth.RequireBearerToken`,
    RFC 9728 handler), with a minimal **fosite v0.49.0** AS: DCR, PKCE S256, opaque HMAC tokens, refresh rotation and RFC 7009
    revoke.
  - Login is delegated to Google via go-oidc (code + PKCE + nonce). The allowlist checks the verified email
    (`MCP_ALLOWED_EMAILS`), and the `hello` tool returns a hashed user id and display name.
  - Revocation: `go run . revoke <email>|--all` bumps a per-user generation in the gitignored `.data/generations.json`. It
    takes effect on the next request, for both access and refresh tokens.
  - 20 unit tests (pass under `-race`): allowlist, 401 / `WWW-Authenticate`, metadata, strict DCR redirect validation,
    non-allowlisted / unverified rejection, hello and then revoke, refresh rotation, per-user vs `--all` revoke, refresh
    token as bearer → 401, token without the `mcp` scope → 403, PKCE required before Google, wrong verifier, pending cap,
    consent page and consent CSRF / deny / replay, generation check fails closed.
  - Review fixes (agy FIX, 4 findings, all fixed; see `_reviews/M0-2a.md` Builder response):
    - Access tokens only, and the `mcp` scope is required.
    - Strict redirect URIs, plus a CSRF-protected consent page showing `client_name` and the redirect host.
    - PKCE is checked before Google, and pending sign-ins are capped.
    - The generation check fails closed.
    - Server timeouts, one shared MCP server with a session timeout, and `/mcp` added to `.gitignore`.
  - `docs/build/spikes/mcp.md`: SDK comparison, OAuth choice, endpoints and flow, token format and lifetime, revocation,
    client table (VERIFIED/UNVERIFIED with sources), local e2e results, M0-2b checklist, recommendation, impact on §4.
- Acceptance:
  - `go run .` serves; `curl -i localhost:8080/mcp` → 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=…`; both
    well-known docs valid JSON → **pass** (shown in mcp.md §7).
  - Real Google sign-in by Brendan via Claude Code (`/mcp` → Authenticate), then `hello` →
    `{"display_name":"Brendan Ashton","user_id":"u_9f51ae389a5c"}` → **pass**. Non-allowlisted rejection
    → **pass** by test (`TestNonAllowlistedAccountRejected`, which includes an empty allowlist).
  - Revocation: live `revoke`, then the same token → `POST /mcp -> 401`, and its refresh → `400 invalid_grant`. Also
    `TestHelloThenRevoke` → **pass**.
  - `mcp.md` has every Scope section, with labels and cited sources → **pass**.
  - Branch diff secret scan: client id, client secret and allowlisted email values each found 0 times. Token / `GOCSPX-` /
    `googleusercontent` patterns: 0. The only email-like string is the test fixture `Alice@Example.com` → **pass**.
  - Re-check after the review fixes: on a fresh `go run .`, the 401 carries `scope="mcp"`; bad DCR URIs → 400; authorize
    without PKCE → `invalid_request` to the client (not Google) → **pass**. The Google leg is unchanged, so no new live
    sign-in.
  - `cd spikes/mcp && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` green. Root `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` green →
    **pass**.
- Deviations from brief:
  - I used Claude Code instead of MCP Inspector, because auto-mode blocked `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector` as
    external code. The brief allows Claude Code ("or Claude Code"). The scratch `--scope local` registration was removed
    afterwards.
  - The non-allowlisted case is shown by test (which the brief allows), not with a second real account.
  - The spike `go.mod` declares `go 1.26.0`, pulled up by its dependencies. The toolchain auto-downloads it.
